runs.title: Miss Universe 2026 final: date, time and how to watch
runs.prompt: The Miss Universe 2026 pageant final is happening today, Monday 24 November 2026, in San Juan, Puerto Rico. Find out: (1) what time the final starts (give it in US Eastern Time and UK time), (2) how someone in the US and someone in the UK can watch it (which channel/streaming service), and (3) who is hosting. Start at the official Miss Universe website and the Wikipedia article, then follow links to confirm the details from at least one news source.
runs.answer:
Heads-up first: every source I read dates the final to Tuesday 24 November 2026, not Monday — TV News Check says REELZ airs it "live on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 8 p.m. ET and 5 p.m. PT," and Google News' feed is stamped Tue, 24 Nov 2026. That 8:00 p.m. ET start equals 1:00 a.m. GMT on Wednesday 25 November in the UK.

US viewing: REELZ carries the English-language broadcast live (cable, satellite and streaming packages, the REELZ+ app, or a live all-access membership via YouTube @Reelzchannel). Wikipedia's Broadcast section also lists Telemundo (Spanish-language) plus Roku and TV Azteca, and says it was made available to stream on Peacock.

Hosting: Mario Lopez and former Miss Universe R'Bonney Gabriel are the presenters, with Zuri Hall and Dayanara Torres providing commentary; Denise Quiñones hosts the preliminaries and Zuleyka Rivera the national costume show, with Jai Rodriguez appearing on each show.

Caveat on part 2: I could not confirm a UK broadcaster or UK streaming route within my page budget — the confirmed platforms are all US-facing, so a UK viewer's options aren't verified here.

I could not independently verify the ~1,500 job-cut figure or any specific closure date, so treat those as unconfirmed.

runs.title: Ukraine's sea-drone strike off Libya: what was hit
runs.prompt: Ukraine says it used naval drones to strike two Russian naval vessels off the coast of Libya in late November 2026. Find out: (1) which ships were hit and whether any was sunk, (2) where exactly off Libya the attack happened, and (3) what Ukraine's president (Zelensky) has said about it. Use non-paywalled sources such as AP News, CBS News, The Guardian, and The Hill.
runs.answer: Ukraine's strike hit the Russian navy corvette Merkury (commissioned in 2023) and the dry cargo ship MV Angara; the Merkury was sunk — satellite imagery showed it capsized and mostly underwater — while the Angara was damaged, not sunk, and a Ka-27 helicopter aboard the corvette was destroyed. The attack took place at Benghazi's port in eastern Libya in the early hours of Sunday 22 November 2026, roughly 1,700 km (1,050 miles) from Ukraine's southern coast. Zelensky, who said seven domestically made naval drones were used, praised the operation as "exemplary," saying: "Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk. It's one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023," adding "We continue our operations in designated waters," and that the Angara was being used by Moscow to transport weapons.

He also said he "kinda knew it was coming," was "super excited to get a new opportunity in a new team," that he never asked out of Vancouver ("I obviously wanted to be in Vancouver... It's never a bad thing to start over somewhere, start fresh"), and that he prides himself on "playing the right way and working really hard and having good details."

runs.title: Pick the clearest NY loan-forgiveness source
runs.prompt: Several outlets are covering New York State's newly opened student-loan-forgiveness programs (up to $50,000). Which of these candidate pages gives the clearest, most usable answer to 'who qualifies and how do they apply' for a normal reader, with the fewest paywalls or agent-blocking walls? Visit each, assess readability and completeness, and pick ONE winner with a one-line reason.
runs.answer: Winner: hesc.ny.gov — the official NYS Higher Education Services Corporation loan-forgiveness pages load with no paywall, cookie wall, or bot challenge and lay out eligibility criteria, award amounts, and the application path in plain language, while linking out to each individual program (the index flags which ones are currently "Accepting Applications"). By contrast, syracuse.com returned HTTP 403 ("Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker") and informnny.com returned "Access to this page has been denied" — the informnny article was only readable in its AMP/proxy version, and even then it summarized eligibility but did little more than tell readers to apply through HESC. Note the HESC URL supplied here is the "Get on Your Feet" program page; for the up-to-$50,000 programs (e.g., Young Farmers, nurses) start at https://hesc.ny.gov/find-aid-you-need/new-york-state-loan-forgiveness-programs and open the specific program.

runs.title: Pick the clearest Libya drone-strike source
runs.prompt: Several outlets are reporting on Ukraine's naval-drone attack on Russian ships off Libya in late November 2026. Which of these candidate pages gives the clearest, most complete account (what was hit, where, and Ukraine's claim) that is actually readable without a paywall or bot wall? Visit each, then pick ONE winner with a one-line reason.
runs.answer: Winner: The Guardian. Its 23 Nov 2026 report is fully readable and complete: Ukraine's SBU confirmed it launched seven domestically made naval drones from a mothership, sinking the new Russian corvette Merkury at its berth in the Benghazi naval base (eastern Libya) and also hitting the dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said was carrying weapons — an operation ~1,500 miles (2,400 km) from the frontline, which he called "exemplary." The AP page was blocked by a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." bot wall and The Hill by a 403 access-denied wall, so neither was usable.
